response:
Pointwise convergence of a sequence of polynomials B_n(x) to f(x) on [0, 1] does not necessarily imply uniform convergence.

Consider the sequence of polynomials B_n(x) = x^n. This sequence converges pointwise to f(x) = 0 on [0, 1], but it does not converge uniformly. In fact, the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges uniformly to 0 on [0, 1] only if n is sufficiently large.

To see why pointwise convergence does not imply uniform convergence, consider the following counterexample:

Let B_n(x) = x^n and f(x) = 0. Then B_n(x) converges pointwise to f(x) on [0, 1], but B_n(x) does not converge uniformly to f(x) on [0, 1]. In fact, for any fixed n, the sequence B_n(x) = x^n converges uniformly to 0 on [0, 1] only if x < 1/n.

In general, pointwise convergence of a sequence of functions to a function f does not imply uniform convergence. Uniform convergence requires that the sequence of functions converges to f at the same rate for all points in the domain, whereas pointwise convergence only requires that the sequence converges to f at each individual point.
